div.head: Had 1.1
div.ab: And eallum Godes freondum gebirað swiðe rihte, þæt hi Godes cirican lufian ⁊ wurðian ⁊ Godes þeowas friðian ⁊ nerian.
⁊ eallum Godes freondum gebyrað swiðe rihte, þæt hi Godes ciricean lufian ⁊ wurðion ⁊ Godes þeowas fryðion ⁊ nerion.
⁊ eallum Godes freondum gebyreþ swyþe rihte, þæt hi Godes cyrcan lufian ⁊ wurþian ⁊ Godes þeowas friðian ⁊ griþian.
Et omnibus amicis Dei recte pertinet, ut sanctam ecclesiam diligant et honorent et Dei ministros pacificare et defendere (custodire) gaudeant.
And eallum Godes freondum gebyreð swyðe rihte þæt hi Godes cyrcan lufian and wurðian, and Godes þeowas friðian and griþian.
Und für alle Freunde Gottes gebührt sich sehr ordentlich, dass sie Gottes Kirche lieben und ehren und die Gottesdiener in Frieden schirmen und schützen (mit Sonderschutz umgeben H).
And it is very right for all God's friends that they love and honour God's church, and shelter God's servants in peace and protect them (surround them with special protection, H).
And to all friends of God it belongs very rightly that they love and honour God’s church and protect and defend God’s servants.
And it is most rightly proper for all friends of God that they love God’s Church and venerate it, and preserve and protect God’s servants.
div.note: H's ‘hi’ was altered to ‘hy’. K: a double space removed. Liebermann compares I Cn 4.; U: checked against Whitelock, EHD I (1979), and corrected (before: ‘And to all friends of God it belongs rightly that they love and honour God's church and protect and defend God's servants.’).

This phrase for ‘good Christian’ also occurs in VIII Atr 1, 1 = I Cn 2, 3. Episc 8

Am nächsten zu VI Atr 45. Die Lesart H lag auch Q vor, denn er übs. mehrfach friðian ⁊ griðian : pacificare et custodire. Und sie stand in Cnut. Dennoch liest vielleicht DO originaler, weil nerian seltener und archaischer, während hq das reimende Lehnwort, um 1050 aus vielen Homilien geläufig, leichter einschwärzen konnte. Es steht u. 11, wahrscheinlich auch Nachtrag.—Vgl. Gl Kirche 5; Geistliche 15

Closest to VI Atr 45. Q too had the reading of H before him, for he several times translates friðian ⁊ griðian : pacificare et custodire. And it stood in Cnut. Nevertheless DO perhaps has the more original reading, because nerian is rarer and more archaic, whereas hq could more easily slip in the rhyming loanword, familiar c. 1050 from many homilies. It occurs below 11, probably also an addition. — Cf. Gl Kirche 5; Geistliche 15
